art_coverage.method: Weapon/Costume 'IconSprite' field values matched Unity Sprite object names by EXACT string equality (no fuzzy matching needed) -- e.g. WeaponData.IconSprite='W_Dagger' exactly matches a Sprite named 'W_Dagger'. Every sprite was exported via Sprite.image (correctly cropped from its atlas), saved as assets/img/weapons/<weapon id>.png and assets/img/heroes/<costume id>.png. Weapon icons are ~70x80px; hero icons are ~177x188px (native exported resolution, not resized).

field_mapping_notes: Every field with a value found in the Locale table's 'key' column gets a companion '<Field>_en' key holding the resolved English string (e.g. Name -> Name_en). Original localization-key fields (e.g. 'WEAPON_NAME_WOODEN_DAGGER') are kept as-is so other languages could be resolved later from Locale.json if wanted -- Locale.json itself was NOT written to data/ (only used as a lookup source); re-run convert_data.py logic against it if other languages are needed.

Comma-separated string fields (declared type 'string' but containing commas, e.g. Costume_Skill_List='0,10053,10054', WeaponCategoryData.Class_OptionType) were split into JSON arrays, with each element cast to int/float where it looked numeric. Fields with only one value stayed as a plain scalar (see WeaponCategoryData id 2 vs id 1 above -- inconsistent array-vs-scalar shape for the same field across rows is a real quirk of the source data, not a conversion bug -- UI code should normalize single values into a length-1 array defensively.
WeaponData/CostumeData 'id' is the stable identifier used for image filenames (assets/img/weapons/<id>.png, assets/img/heroes/<id>.png).

WeaponLevelDPSData (19 rows, id 1-19) and WeaponLevelUpGoldCostData (20 rows) are NOT per-weapon-per-level tables -- they look like small reference/tier lookup curves (id appears to double as a level or tier index, not a weapon id.) BalancingData_Rarity is where the real per-rarity DPS growth formula lives: fields WeaponDPSAdd, WeaponDPSMult, WeaponDPS_LevelUpAdd, MaxLevel are keyed by Rarity (1-14 seen -- more rarity tiers than the 6 named in earlier analysis, worth double-checking against WeaponData.Rarity's actual value range). Cross-reference WeaponRandomDPSRange too before assuming the exact upgrade-stat formula -- I did not fully reverse-engineer the formula itself, only confirmed where the relevant raw numbers live. This needs verification/formula-derivation before the UI's 'upgrade' feature can show numerically-accurate adjusted stats.

CostumeStarGradeOptionData has null OptionType/OptionValue on some rows (e.g. Star_Grade 1 in group 100001) where OptionStyle=3 and only a text-only unlock description exists (e.g. a skill-unlock flavor row with no numeric stat bonus) -- treat OptionType/OptionValue nulls as 'no numeric stat bonus at this star grade' rather than a data gap.

TraitOptionTypeData/_en description fields contain a '{0}' placeholder for the actual percentage/value to interpolate in at render time (e.g. 'Total Attack Power +{0}%') -- the numeric value to substitute comes from TraitOptionData, not this table.
